items.question: How does PDF conversion work without uploading my documents?
items.answer: Conversion runs 100% on your device using native Rust vector engines and sandboxed document adapters.
items.usage: Select Convert in the sidebar, choose Convert From PDF or Convert To PDF, configure your target format (Office, Image, PDF/A, HTML, TXT), and click Convert.
items.outputs: Generates pristine DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, PNG, JPEG, PDF/A-2b/3b, HTML, or TXT files atomically to your target folder.
items.offlineBoundaries: Zero network requests. No cloud telemetry, no remote servers. Everything runs in isolated local worker processes.

items.question: Can I reorder, rotate, delete, and extract pages safely?
items.answer: Yes. The Organize workspace lets you manipulate pages visually with drag-and-drop page grids and instant non-destructive actions.
items.usage: Drag PDF pages into the visual grid to reorder them, rotate individual or all pages, delete unwanted pages, or split into chapters.
items.outputs: Saves an atomically rewritten, valid PDF file while leaving the original untouched unless explicit overwrite is chosen.
items.offlineBoundaries: All page tree adjustments happen in memory and local temp files; no external runtime dependencies.

items.question: How does PDF compression reduce file size without losing readability?
items.answer: Optimize applies stream deflation, unreferenced font/image resource pruning, and optional bicubic image downsampling.
items.usage: Choose an optimization preset (Lossless, Standard Web, Maximum Compression), preview estimated savings, and apply.
items.outputs: An optimized PDF with preserved vector clarity, stripped duplicate objects, and verified MediaBox dimensions.
items.offlineBoundaries: Strict never-grow failsafe: if compressed output is larger than original, original is kept. No network dependencies.

items.question: How secure is encryption and digital signing in LocalPDF Studio?
items.answer: Security uses military-grade AES-256 and AES-128 encryption with strict fail-closed cryptographic integrity and PKCS#12 signing.
items.usage: Set user and owner passwords, configure granular print/copy permissions, or select a PKCS#12 (.p12/.pfx) digital certificate to sign.
items.outputs: Standard-compliant encrypted PDF or PAdES digitally signed document with cryptographically verifiable digests.
items.offlineBoundaries: Passwords and private keys are zeroized in RAM immediately after use. No remote timestamp authority pings or certificate upload.

items.question: Can I add annotations, watermarks, stamps, and bates numbering?
items.answer: Yes. The Edit suite allows adding standard PDF markup annotations, headers/footers, text overlays, and legal bates numbers.
items.usage: Open a PDF in Edit mode, select annotation tools (highlight, underline, sticky note, watermark), customize styles, and click Save.
items.outputs: Modified PDF containing standardized ISO 32000-2 annotation dictionaries with preserved document structure.
items.offlineBoundaries: All text layouts, glyph rendering, and annotation structures are synthesized entirely within native Rust libraries.

items.question: How do AcroForm and XFA form filling and flattening work?
items.answer: LocalPDF Studio detects, populates, exports, and flattens form fields (text boxes, checkboxes, radio buttons, dropdowns) seamlessly.
items.usage: Fill out fields interactively, import/export data via XFDF, or choose 'Flatten Form' to convert interactive widgets into static vector art.
items.outputs: Populated interactive PDF or a completely flattened read-only document ready for official submission.
items.offlineBoundaries: AcroForm input data is sanitized against buffer overflows and script injections locally; no web beacons.

items.question: Can I convert Markdown documents to PDF and vice versa?
items.answer: Yes. LocalPDF Studio provides a high-fidelity bidirectional Markdown conversion pipeline with full code highlighting and table support.
items.usage: Type or paste Markdown in the editor with live preview, or import a PDF to extract structured, semantic Markdown headers and lists.
items.outputs: Beautifully typeset vector PDF documents or clean CommonMark markdown files.
items.offlineBoundaries: Rendered completely using offline local typesetting algorithms and syntax highlighters.

items.question: How does the AI Summarizer process text without cloud LLMs?
items.answer: Summaries are created locally using pure extractive algorithms by default, or an optional offline local ONNX/GGUF model.
items.usage: Select extractive mode for instant statistical key-sentence summarization, or import a local GGUF/ONNX model for map-reduce synthesis.
items.outputs: Concise Markdown summaries or structured topic outlines saved to disk.
items.offlineBoundaries: Failsafe F19 enforced: strictly offline local inference. Network socket access is barred via container and OS sandboxing.

items.question: Can I process hundreds of files simultaneously?
items.answer: The Batch Queue manages asynchronous multi-threaded jobs with automatic concurrency scaling based on detected hardware tiers.
items.usage: Enqueue multiple documents or directories, choose individual operations, prioritize tasks, and monitor progress bars.
items.outputs: Batch processed files written atomically to designated destination folders with per-file status reports.
items.offlineBoundaries: Background jobs run on isolated worker threads. Crashes are isolated and cannot corrupt state or exit the application.

items.question: What is tool chaining and how do workflow pipelines work?
items.answer: Workflows let you chain multiple PDF transformations (e.g., OCR -> Redact -> Compress -> Sign) into an automated one-click pipeline.
items.usage: Select a built-in workflow preset (Legal Compliance, Archival, Web Optimization) or build custom pipelines with sequential steps.
items.outputs: A thoroughly processed final PDF that has passed every stage with atomic verification between stages.
items.offlineBoundaries: Pipeline stages pass temporary files using internal WAL journals on disk; zero cloud dependency.
